title: Affine nonvanishing loci imply ampleness
statement: Let $k$ be a field, let $X$ be a proper scheme over $k$ [def-weil-proper-morphism], and let $\mathcal L$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-sc-invertible-module]. For $n\geq1$ and $s\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal L^{\otimes n})$, put $X_s=\{x\in X:s_x\notin\mathfrak m_x(\mathcal L^{\otimes n})_x\}$, where $\mathfrak m_x$ is the maximal ideal of $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ [def-weil-residue-field]. If for every $x\in X$ there are $n\geq1$ and $s$ such that $x$ belongs to the affine open $X_s$, then $\mathcal L$ is ample in the sense of [def-sc-ample]: some positive tensor power of $\mathcal L$ has a complete linear system giving a closed immersion into projective space over $k$.

source.place: Properties, Definition 01PS (definition-ample): the affine nonvanishing-locus criterion; Morphisms, Lemma 01VT (lemma-finite-type-over-affine-ample-very-ample), (1) implies (5), with base Spec(k), using Lemma 01VK (lemma-ample-over-affine). Since X is proper and projective space is separated, the resulting immersion is closed. The complete-linear-system morphism is also a closed immersion: extend its finite defining sections to a basis of H^0(X,L^d), project back to the original linear system on the open where those coordinates do not simultaneously vanish, and use properness to make this immersion closed.

proof.text: Properness over the field $k$ includes finite type and quasi-compactness. The assumed affine nonvanishing loci therefore satisfy the two conditions of the absolute ampleness definition [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module], so $\mathcal L$ is ample in that sense.

Apply the affine-base ample-to-immersion theorem [lem-weil-pbc-ample-very-ample-immersion-affine-base] with $A=k$ and the structure morphism $X\to\operatorname{Spec}(k)$. It gives $d\ge1$, a projective-space immersion $j$ and an isomorphism $\mathcal L^{\otimes d}\cong j^*\mathcal O(1)$. Over a field this projective-space model is the usual $\mathbf P^N_k$ model used in [def-sc-ample].

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma 01VT, implication (1) => (5), with base Spec(k), and Constructions Definition 01NF

proof.text: The structure morphism $q_n:P_n\to\operatorname{Spec}(k)$ of projective space over $k$ is separated [lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-proj-separated]. Since $X\to\operatorname{Spec}(k)$ is proper and $q_n\circ j$ is the structure morphism of $X$, the immersion $j$ is proper by the proper-to-separated lemma [lem-weil-pbc-proper-to-separated]. A proper immersion is a closed immersion [lem-weil-pbc-proper-immersion-closed]. Put $\mathcal M=\mathcal L^{\otimes d}$ and let $s_0,\dots,s_n\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal M)$ be the images of the coordinate sections $j^*x_0,\dots,j^*x_n$ under $j^*\mathcal O(1)\cong\mathcal M$; by the functor of points of projective space [lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-functor-of-points] $j$ is the morphism associated with $(\mathcal M,(s_0,\dots,s_n))$. Let $V\subseteq\Gamma(X,\mathcal M)$ be their $k$-span. The morphism $j_V:X\to\mathbf P(V^\vee)_k$ associated with $V$, followed by the linear embedding $\lambda:\mathbf P(V^\vee)_k\to P_n$ dual to $k^{n+1}\to V$, $e_l\mapsto s_l$ (a closed immersion, hence separated [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-integral-separated-uc] (a)), is $j$; so $j_V$ is a closed immersion [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-from-composite], with $j_V^*\mathcal O(1)\cong\mathcal M$.

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma 01W6 and Lemma 01VT; Schemes, Lemma 01IQ; Constructions, Lemma 01NE (morphisms to projective space)

proof.text: Apply [lem-pc-complete-linear-system-closed] to $X$, $\mathcal M=\mathcal L^{\otimes d}$ and the subspace $V$ of step 3: the complete linear system $\Gamma(X,\mathcal L^{\otimes d})$ gives a closed immersion into projective space over $k$ pulling $\mathcal O(1)$ back to $\mathcal L^{\otimes d}$. So $\mathcal L^{\otimes d}$ is very ample and $\mathcal L$ is ample in the sense of [def-sc-ample], since $d\ge1$.
